title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: Your makerspace code handles each booking question in the same three steps: a model call pulls the machine and date out of the message, the code itself calls check_calendar with them, and a second model call writes the reply. Which description fits best?

options.text: An agent, because it calls the model more than once per request
A workflow, because the code fixes the order of the steps
An agent, because it uses a calendar tool to fetch live facts
Neither, because an agent needs more than a single tool to count

items.stem: In one sentence, what is the difference between a workflow and an agent in terms of who decides what happens next?

Whenever a student confirms a booking, the assistant must always do the same four things in this order: check the training record, check the calendar, write the booking, send the confirmation email. Which design is the better choice for this part of the assistant?

options.text: An agent, because the booking involves several different tools
An agent, because students word their requests in many ways
An agent, because a model can reorder the steps if one fails
A workflow, because the steps and their order are known in advance

items.stem: To keep the arithmetic simple, assume every model call costs $0.01. A fixed workflow for answering one question always makes exactly 2 model calls. An agent for the same question averages 5 model calls. How many more dollars would the agent cost than the workflow over 1,000 questions?
Which request to the makerspace assistant is the strongest case for an agent rather than a fixed workflow?

options.text: A student asks why their 3D print keeps failing, and the fix could need any mix of manual lookups and follow-up questions
A student asks whether the laser cutter is free at a date and time they have already given in the message
A student asks to be sent the same confirmation email that follows every booking made through the system
A student asks for the opening hours of the workshop, which are printed in one table in the manual

items.stem: At the design review, a teammate says: "Let's make the whole assistant one agent, since it is the most flexible." Name one thing you give up by letting the model choose the steps on a task whose steps you already know.
